intended_object: Strict cardinality comparison |x| < |y| between two sets x, y, stated inside a model M of set theory: there is an injection from x into y but no bijection between them. Inferred from the name, from the neighbouring definitions `cardLE` and `cardEq`, and from the lemma `cardLT_iff`.
explanation:
The body is `cardLE x y ∧ ¬cardEq x y`. Here `cardLE` means that some element f of `Func x y` is an injective function, and `cardEq` means that some f ∈ `Func x y` is injective with range y, i.e. a bijection from x onto y. So `cardLT` says x injects into y but is not equinumerous with it. That is the textbook definition of |x| < |y|, written as a relation inside the structure M so that it can be expressed as a first-order formula (this is what the `@[realize]` attribute is for).

The library proves `cardLT_iff : cardLT x y ↔ #x < #y`, which confirms it matches Mathlib's `Cardinal` order. The degenerate cases come out right: for x = y = ∅ the empty function is a bijection, so `cardLT ∅ ∅` is false, and `cardLT ∅ y` holds exactly when y is nonempty.

Mathlib has no `def` of the same internal relation for an abstract model of set theory. The closest notion is the `<` order on `Cardinal`, and `cardLT_iff` connects the two.

The setting is a general `ZFStructure M`, which is the natural setting for an internal set-theoretic notion. The definition is therefore not too narrow.
